en.title: Lanterns Finale Hints at Hal Jordan's Comic Return as The Spectre
en.summary: The Lanterns TV series finale left fans reeling with Hal Jordan's apparent death, but a path to his comic book resurrection is clearer than ever. Could the fallen hero return as a divine force?
en.body:
The final moments of the **Lanterns** TV series delivered a gut punch: **Hal Jordan** is dead, seemingly for good. After a season spent unraveling a mystery that spanned a decade, the finale saw **Hal** meet his end not by an alien threat, but by a bullet from **Kerry**, who sought to prevent him from acting against **Noah**. This stark reality, devoid of cosmic battles, felt like a deliberate departure from the expected superhero fare.

Even the **Hal-o-Gram**, the digital echo that allowed **John Stewart** to continue interacting with his friend, dissipated, making **Hal’s** expiration feel absolute. Yet, for those familiar with the deep lore of the Green Lanterns in the comics, this seemingly final end might just be the beginning of a familiar, albeit darker, chapter. The show has consistently played with deviations from the source material, but the potential for **Hal Jordan's** return echoes a pivotal moment in comic history.

## A Path Paved in Redemption

In the comics, **Hal Jordan's** journey from hero to villain and back is one of the most dramatic arcs in DC history. Following the destruction of Coast City during the **Death of Superman** storyline, **Hal** descended into madness, becoming the power-hungry entity known as **Parallax**. He destroyed the Green Lantern Corps, killed his friend **Kilowog**, and waged war against his former allies. This dark period culminated in the **1994** storyline **Emerald Twilight** and the subsequent line-wide soft-reboot **Zero Hour**.

However, redemption arrived in **1996's** company-wide crossover **The Final Night**. Faced with an extinction-level threat as the Sun-Eater consumed Earth's sun, **Hal** made the ultimate sacrifice. In a selfless act, he poured all his remaining energy into reigniting the sun, reciting his oath one last time. This act of pure heroism, despite his past transgressions, earned **Hal Jordan** a chance at absolution, paving the way for him to become the divine wrath of God – **The Spectre**.

## What This Means for Fans

The **Lanterns** finale, by leaving **Hal Jordan** dead but not *truly* gone from the narrative's potential, opens the door for this iconic comic storyline to be adapted. While the show has taken liberties, this particular arc—redemption through self-sacrifice and a subsequent divine transformation—is a cornerstone of **Hal's** character. The absence of an otherworldly threat in the finale, focusing instead on deeply personal stakes and relationships, highlights the show's unique approach. This sets up a fascinating question for fans: will the series embrace the cosmic scale of **Hal's** comic resurrection, or will it find a new, perhaps more grounded, way for him to return?

## What's Next

Details regarding future seasons or potential spin-offs that would explore **Hal Jordan's** fate have not yet been announced. Fans will be eagerly awaiting any news on whether the **Lanterns** series will delve into the divine wrath of **The Spectre** or forge a new path for the fallen hero.

content_raw: This article contains spoilers for Lanterns . Ever since the pilot episode of Lanterns ended with a shot of Hal Jordan, frozen on a high school football field stand and dead from a bullet hole in his head, fans have hoped against hope that the death would be undone. Yet, despite the fact that Lanterns takes place in a world with robot Manhunters and magical wishing rings, the finale ended not only with Hal still dead, but the Hal-o-Gram backup that allowed him to pal around with John Stewart dissipating once and for all. Yet, as final and the finale seemed to treat Hal Jordan’s expiration—and as many deviations from the comics taken by the show—it does leave open a path to return. The Hal Jordan of the DCU could return in the same way he did in the comics, by becoming the Spectre, the living manifestation of God’s wrath. Before talking about the Spectre, we have to go back to the conditions of Hal’s death. As discussed in previous articles, Hal Jordan goes mad when Coast City is destroyed during the Death of Superman storyline. By the end of the 1994 storyline Emerald Twilight , Hal has destroyed the Corps, killed his friend Kilowog, and become the supervillain Parallax. For a while, Parallax is a big bad for new Green Lantern Kyle Rayner and the DC Universe in general, even rewriting for the line-wide soft-reboot Zero Hour . But by 1996, Hal’s villain journey came to an end. In that year’s company-wide crossover The Final Night , Earth’s heroes must work together to prevent a Sun-Eater from consuming our sun. In a final desperate move, Hal expels all of his power to reignite the sun, reciting his oath as he sacrifices himself. Despite all that he had done wrong, that one act of selflessness was enough to earn Hal Jordan a chance at redemption by becoming the Spectre. Although not an A-list character, the Spectre actually goes back further than Hal Jordan and the entire Green Lantern concept. Created by Jerry Siegel and Bernard Baily for 1940’s More Fun Comics #52, the Spectre came to be when tough cop Jim Corrigan is murdered by thugs, but he is revived by a divine force to enforce justice on Earth. In his earliest stories, the Spectre played like a standard superhero, with Corrigan transforming into a white-skinned figure in a green cloak and underpants to punch bad guys and save the innocent. Fighting alongside the Justice Society of America , the Spectre wasn’t above killing a goon by aging them to a skeleton in a matter of seconds, but he was more or less heroic. However, throughout the Silver Age and Bronze Age, the Spectre became more macabre, something like a heroic Freddy Krueger . He manifested a giant pair of scissors to cut down a baddie, turned killers into candles to let them melt to death, or transformed heroin addicts into the tips of his fingers so he could inject them with fire.
